recentItems.title: RATKO MLADIC FUNERAL LIVE: Thousands Gather in Belgrade Following Death of Mladic at 84 | Watch LIVE
recentItems.description:
RATKO MLADIC FUNERAL LIVE | Thousands Gather in Belgrade Following Death of Mladic at 84 | World News LIVE

 LIVE from Belgrade, Serbia, where crowds of supporters gather for the funeral of former Bosnian Serb military commander Ratko Mladic, who died last month aged 84 while held at a UN detention facility in The Hague. Mladic was convicted by an international tribunal of genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes committed during the 1992–95 Bosnian War.


BELGRADE — Thousands of mourners gathered in the Serbian capital on Monday for the funeral of former Bosnian Serb military commander Ratko Mladic, who died on August 27, 2026, at the age of 84 while serving a life sentence for genocide and war crimes in The Hague. The body of the convicted general, flown back on a government plane, lay in state at the Church of St. Luke in Vidikovac before a scheduled burial at Belgrade's Topcider Cemetery. The events have triggered severe diplomatic friction, leading EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos to postpone an official visit to Serbia due to what she termed the 'glorification' of a war criminal. While Mladic remains a highly revered figure among many Serbian nationalists, international bodies and victims' families have strongly condemned the public honors, highlighting the enduring ethnic divisions in the Balkans decades after the 1990s Yugoslav wars.
